newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil '96 oper deficit figure reliable - cenbank.
newsitem.headline: Brazil '96 oper deficit figure reliable - cenbank.

text.p: Brazil's 3.89 percent of gross domestic product operational public sector deficit last year is a reliable figure and no expenditure was deliberately carried over to 1997, a Central Bank official said.

Altamir Lopes, head of the bank's economics department, told reporters some 13th month salary payments had been delayed to this year by some states and municipalities, but he expected the public finances to continue to improve in 1997.
"The 3.89 percent deficit figure is absolutely reliable," he said, adding "absolutely nothing" had been carried over to 1997 to make last year's fiscal performance appear more rosy.
"The drop was much better (last year than in 1995)," Lopes said, attributing it to "evident spending constraints".
-- Lopes also noted that federal tax receipts were a record 10 billion reais in December, which improved the government's accounts.
-- Lopes said the states and municipalities continued to improve their fiscal performance, cutting their primary deficit to 0.57 percent of GDP in December from 0.69 percent of GDP the month before.
-- Real interest payments in December were 28.5 billion reais or 3.79 percent of GDP compared with 34 billion reais or 5.14 percent of GDP the previous year.
In November, real interest payments amounted to 3.94 percent of GDP.
"The reduction in the real interest rates was small, but contributed to a better operational result," Lopes said.
The primary result does not include debt servicing, while the operational result does.
